definitions.explanation: written symbols used to separate sentences and clarify meaning, particularly the period and comma

examples.japanese: {句読点|くとうてん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{正|ただ}しく→正しい：00893_tadashii⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
⟦{文章|ぶんしょう}→文章：02957_bunshou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{適切|てきせつ}→適切：01621_tekisetsu⟧な{句読点|くとうてん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧だ。

examples.english: The placement of punctuation can change the meaning of a sentence.

notes:
JAPANESE PUNCTUATION:
{句読点|くとうてん} specifically refers to:
- ⟦{句点|くてん}→句点：19157_kuten⟧（。）- period (full stop)
- ⟦{読点|とうてん}→読点：16992_touten⟧（、）- comma

OTHER PUNCTUATION MARKS:
- 「 」- ⟦{括弧|かっこ}→括弧：00151_kakko⟧ (quotation marks/brackets)
- ？ - ⟦{疑問符|ぎもんふ}→疑問符：24302_gimonfu⟧ (question mark)
- ！ - {感嘆符|かんたんふ} (exclamation mark)
- ・ - {中点|なかてん} (middle dot)
- … - {三点|さんてん}⟦リーダー→リーダー：24312_riidaa⟧ (ellipsis)

USAGE:
- Japanese uses 。 and 、 instead of . and ,
- Vertical text traditionally uses different punctuation placement
- Formal writing follows specific rules for {句読点|くとうてん}

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {句読点|くとうてん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧ - to add punctuation
